ruleName: When in doubt about the rules
title: What should you do if you’re unsure which rule applies (stroke play)?
question: In stroke play, if you’re unsure about what the rules require and can’t find help straight away, what is the correct thing to do?

choices.text: Play two balls, record both scores, and ask an official afterwards
Guess a rule and continue playing
Ignore the situation and move on
Mark your ball and wait for a referee without finishing the hole

explanation: If you’re in doubt about a rule in stroke play, play two balls (declaring which you want to count before doing so), finish the hole with both, then get a ruling before submitting your score.

juniorVersion.title: What should you do if you are not sure about the rules when you play a hole?
juniorVersion.question: You are playing a golf hole and something happens that you're not sure about. You can't find any adult or official to ask what to do. What should you do?

choices.text: Play two balls on the hole, write both scores, and ask an adult or referee what to do after
Guess what you think is the right rule and keep playing
Just forget about it and carry on playing
Put a marker down by your ball and wait for the referee without finishing the hole

juniorVersion.explanation: If you are not sure which rule to use and no one can help you right away, you should play two balls all the way to the hole. Write down your scores with both balls, then ask a referee or an adult what to do before you hand in your scorecard.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A person who helps everyone follow the golf rules.
A small object you put on the green to show where your ball was.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Give a pretend example where a child is unsure if their ball is in a puddle or not, and show how to play two balls from that spot with clear instructions.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they can just guess a rule or ignore the problem and keep playing.
They might think they must wait and stop playing unless a referee is there.
